title: papio browser bridge message v1
description: One framed native-messaging envelope between the MV3 extension and the papio native host. Locked protocol papio-browser/1. Metadata only — PDF bytes and secrets never cross this channel; encoded messages are capped at 262144 bytes; integers are capped at JavaScript's exact range; unknown types, fields, and null object members are rejected (fail closed). auth_pending/auth_returned deliberately have no URL/title fields: identity-provider addresses never leave the browser.

origin_hint.description: A bare https origin with a lowercase host: charset/case is byte-identical to internal/protocol/protocol.go's originHostRE and extension/src/protocol.ts's ORIGIN_HOST_RE. Case is rejected, not normalized (e.g. https://EXAMPLE.com is invalid). Label count is deliberately unconstrained: internal/config/config.go's validateOpenURLBase accepts any non-empty https host, so a single-label intranet resolver origin (e.g. https://library) is a legitimate deployment and MUST validate here too — do not re-tighten this pattern to require two-or-more labels. This is the published contract: validateResolverOriginHint must never accept a value this pattern rejects. It agrees with the TypeScript parser only over the DNS-shaped subset a genuine producer emits — a purely numeric single-label host (e.g. https://123, reparsed as an IPv4 literal by the WHATWG URL parser) and a zero-padded port (e.g. :08443, normalized by new URL(...)) both match this pattern but fail TypeScript's round-trip check; neither shape is reachable from a genuine producer. See validateResolverOriginHint's doc comment for the full accepted-gap list.

page_host.description: A bounded lowercase hostname that must not start or end with '.' and must not contain '..' — the 'not' clause encodes the same three rejections internal/protocol/protocol.go's DeliveryContextPayload.validate and extension/src/protocol.ts perform explicitly alongside this pattern.
